title: Make yourself at home
briefing: Time to build something of your own.
tips: `mkdir NAME` makes a directory. `touch NAME` creates an empty file.
`~` means your home directory from anywhere: ~/projects is /home/player/projects.
objective: In your home directory, create a directory named `projects`, and inside it an empty file named `todo.txt`.
hints: You need two things: a directory, then a file inside it. There is one command for each.
`mkdir` makes directories and `touch` creates empty files. `~/` means your home from anywhere.

reactions.say: Directory: done. Now the file inside it.
todo.txt landed in your home directory, not inside projects. Paths are relative to where you stand — `mv todo.txt projects/` would move it.

explanation: `mkdir` creates directories, `touch` creates empty files. `~/projects/todo.txt` works from anywhere; `projects/todo.txt` only works when you are in ~. Bonus: `mkdir -p a/b/c` creates a whole chain at once.
